records.subject: Demand for release of Tamil Nadu fishermen detained in Sri Lankan prisons.
records.SM_Text:
Shri I.S. Inbadurai:

I seek to draw attention of the Government towards the safety and early release of Tamil Nadu fishermen detained in Sri Lankan prisons. At present, 38 Tamil Nadu fishermen are reportedly lodged in various prisons in Sri Lanka, including Welikada and Jaffna. The situation inside several Sri Lankan prisons is a matter of grave concern. Recent violence at Negombo prison resulted in the deaths of more than 25 people and left over 100 injured. Tragically, an Indian national, also lost his life in the unrest. Following this incident, it is reported that a large number of prisoners have been transferred to facilities in the Northern and Eastern Provinces, including Jaffna. This has further heightened concerns about the safety and security of those detained. In this volatile environment, the continued detention of our fishermen poses a serious risk to their lives and well-being. Already separated from their families and livelihoods, they must not be exposed to further danger from prison violence and unrest.  Therefore, I urge the  Government to intervene at diplomatic level with the Government of Sri Lanka and ensure:  1.  Immediate safety and protection of all Tamil Nadu fishermen detained in Sri Lankan prisons; 2.  Their early release and repatriation, wherever legally feasible; and  3.  Immediate consular access and regular welfare monitoring of every detained fisherman until their safe return to India.

(ENDS)

records.subject: Concern over disturbances in LPG gas supply.
Concern over issues faced by Tamil fishermen.
records.SM_Text:
Shri I.S. Inbadurai: I draw attention of the Government to the recurring and deeply distressing issue faced by Tamil fishermen. Fishermen from the coastal districts of Tamil Nadu venture into the sea only to earn their daily livelihood, yet they are repeatedly arrested, harassed and have their boats, nets and equipment confiscated. This is not merely a law-and-order issue; it is a humanitarian and livelihood concern affecting thousands of families who depend solely on fishing. In the last ten years alone, more than 1,500 Tamil fishermen have been arrested and over 500 fishing boats have been seized by the Sri Lankan Navy. These boats and fishing equipment, worth several crores of rupees, are the sole assets of poor fishing families. Their seizure pushes entire households into debt, insecurity, and distress. A permanent and sustainable solution to this long-pending issue is needed. Temporary diplomatic interventions are no longer sufficient. What is required is a clear, mutually agreed common resolution with the Government of Sri Lanka, including precise demarcation of marine boundaries and practical fishing arrangements that respect traditional fishing rights. I urge the Government to take this matter with Sri Lanka to evolve an amicable, humane and lasting solution, ensuring the safety, dignity and protection of our fishermen and their belongings.

(ENDS)

records.subject: Need for a responsible and forward looking approach for ‘Agniveers’ transition to civilian life.
records.SM_Text:
Shri I.S. Inbadurai: I rise to address the Government on the future of our Agniveers, particularly the first batch recruited under the Agnipath scheme, of which around 40,000 young Agniveers are expected to complete their four-year tenure and exit the Armed Forces in 2026.These young citizens joined the forces at a very early age and served the nation with dedication, discipline, and pride. The government fully recognises its responsibility towards them, not just during service, but equally after their exit. As per the scheme, up to 25 percent of each batch will be given the opportunity for permanent enrolment in the Armed Forces based on merit and performance. The remaining 75 percent will transition to civilian life with a tax-free Seva Nidhi package of about ₹11.71 lakh, providing them financial security at a crucial stage. The government has taken comprehensive steps for their re-employment and reintegration. There is 10 percent reservation for ex-Agniveers in CAPFs and the Ministry of Defence, along with age relaxation. Many states have extended similar benefits in police and public sector jobs.? I urge the Government to ensure Skill certificates, educational support through NIOS and IGNOU, access to credit for entrepreneurship, and a dedicated placement portal through inter-ministerial coordination for Agniveersso as to ensure that their service to the nation becomes a strong foundation for a secure and dignified future.

(ENDS)
